title: What Improved, In My Own Words
objective: Summarise what you learnt across Part A in your own words, checked against the measure you set in week one.

blocks.text: BUILD · Art · Week 3. Trinity Arts Award Bronze. What Improved, In My Own Words.
Objective: summarise what you learnt across Part A in your own words, checked against the measure you set in week one.
Success evidence: your Part A pages in week order, one ring on met, part met or not met, three sentences in your own words, and a locator that names the file, the page and the box.

Everything you write today comes off your own pages. You write about marks, tools, boxes and numbers. You are never asked about your home, your family, your body, how you look or what you believe. Nobody in this room is asked what they believe.
Theme: My Creative Identity. Identity here means what your own artwork keeps choosing.
40 minutes. Offline.

This deck evidences Bronze Part A, Explore the arts as a participant. The register says Part A requires active participation in any art form, improvement, and a summary of what they learnt. This lesson IS that summary; the participation and the improvement were evidenced in the four Part A decks before it. Bronze attempted rule, quoted from the register: "ONE Attempted allowed overall. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass." The evidence file cap for the whole Bronze level is 10 files, so the summary sheet joins the Part A section rather than opening a new file. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication. Bronze is the Level 1 Award in the Arts, qualification number 501/0081/6, and results are Pass or Below Pass only: no grades, no marks language. The register also states that advisers must not write plans, reviews or evidence for pupils, so you may scribe a pupil's words and you may never improve them. The portfolio is digital and organised by part, and an evidence locator names the file plus the page, slide or timecode; "in arts log" is refused as a locator. Claim no number here that is not in the register.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Part A pages out and in week order before pupils sit down. A missing page is found now, not at minute thirty.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil turns to home or family, say: I only need the page and the box number. Then point at the strip and move on.

blocks.text: Three weeks, one part
Part A has taken you three weeks.
In week one you made a baseline piece.
You wrote three words for what it did well.
You wrote one word for what it did not do yet.
Then you wrote a skill card with a measure on it.
In week two you filled a skill strip.
You took one line of feedback and wrote it down.
Last lesson you made the change that line asked for.
Today you say what all of that taught you.
Lay the four Part A artefacts out yourself if a pupil cannot: baseline piece, skill card, skill strip, change record. The lesson does not work from memory.
You need all four of those on your desk.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Say both summaries yourself. Never ask a pupil to model the weak one.

blocks.text: Two summaries, one folder
Watch me sum up the same three weeks twice.
The first time I say I got better at shading.
There is no measure and no page to look at.
The second time I read my measure out first.
My measure says no white gaps in a box.
Then I hold my last box up next to it.
Now you can check me, and that is the whole difference.

items: 1 · lay your pages out in week order.
2 · read the measure you set in week one.
3 · hold your last work against that measure.
4 · write what you learnt, and name the page.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Work through your own four pages on the visualiser. Keep the pupil pages closed while you model.
stages.data-ta2: Say part met out loud at least once. Pupils copy the word they hear you use.

blocks.text: I check my work against my measure
My skill card names one skill: shade a flat tone.
My measure says a box with no white gaps.
First I lay my pages out in week order.
Baseline piece, skill card, skill strip, then the change.
I do not write one word yet.
Next I read the measure out loud, word for word off the card.

boxes.head: READ
boxes.line1: the week one measure, word for word

boxes.head: WRITE
boxes.line1: what you learnt, and the page

blocks.caption: Four steps, and the summary is done
blocks.title: How to summarise Part A
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows, the first holding a small stack of four pages and the third a box held beside a ruled line

blocks.text: Then I hold box eight against the measure.
I look for white gaps, because that is what it asks.
Box eight has two small gaps left in it.
So my measure is part met.
Part met is a real answer here.
It is not a fail, and I write it down.
Last I write three short sentences.
Three sentences: what I set out to do, what my pages show, and what I learnt.
Model the part met verdict on purpose. A room that only ever hears met will write met, and Part A wants the summary honest, not flattering.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Cards face down until every table is still. Turn them over together on your count.

blocks.text: Sort the summaries, then match the missing part
Six summary cards are on your table.
Each card is somebody's summary of Part A.
Sort them into two piles: checked, and not checked.
A checked card names a measure, shows proof and says what was learnt.

items: A · I can shade a box with no white gaps. Box 8 has no gaps. Skill strip, page 3.
B · My work got a lot better this term.
C · I can draw six lines the same width. Box 7 shows six the same. Log page 4.
D · I can hold a line for ten counts. I think I did it.
E · My measure was ten clean marks. Box 8 has ten. Log page 2.
F · I tried hard every week and I never gave up.

blocks.text: Now take the pile that is not checked.
Match each card to the part it is missing.
It is the measure, the proof, or what you learnt.
Every card gets a match, even a guess.
Answer key: A and C are checked. B and F are missing the measure. D is missing the proof, because no page or box is named. E is missing what was learnt. Take the argued card first when you go round.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Hold up a real Part A folder and count the pages out loud, so the hunt is seen and not just described.

blocks.text: Name the page, not the whole folder
Now watch the same summary go wrong.
I write that my proof is in the arts log.
An adult opens the folder and starts hunting.
There are eleven pages in there.
My proof is real, but nobody can find it.
Proof that cannot be found does not count.

boxes.head: NAMED PAGE
boxes.line2: the adult looks once and sees it

boxes.head: IN THE ARTS LOG
boxes.line1: no page, no box, no date
boxes.line2: the adult hunts and gives up

blocks.caption: Same proof, and only one route reaches it
blocks.title: A locator against a folder name
blocks.alt: Two panels side by side, one with a single arrow landing on a numbered box and one with arrows scattering across a stack of pages

blocks.text: So name three things in order: the file, the page, then the box.
Do the same for a photo: name it, and name the part it shows.

items: 1 · name the file, such as skill strip.
2 · name the page number written on it.
3 · name the box or the ring on that page.

blocks.text: A locator is not extra work. It is the proof.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Pair by table, not by choice. Call the swap out loud at the halfway point.
stages.data-ta2: Listen for the word good. Redirect it: ask where the proof sits, not whether the work is nice.

blocks.text: Read your measure to a partner
Work in twos, with your pages out.
Partner one reads their measure out loud.
Partner two asks one question: where is the proof?
Partner one names the file, the page and the box.
If they cannot, they write that down as a job.
Then swap over, with two minutes each way.
You are checking the locator, not the artwork.
You say found it, or not yet.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Scribe on request, word for word. You must not write a pupil's summary for them, and you must not tidy it into a better one.
stages.data-ta2: A pupil stuck on sentence three gets a stem, not an answer: I learnt to ... Then wait.

blocks.text: Write your summary, in your own words
Now write your Part A summary on the sheet.
Start by copying your measure into the first box.
Copy it word for word off your skill card.
Do not write it from memory.
Then ring one word of three: met, part met, not met.
Hold your last box against the measure first.
Then write three short sentences under the ring.
Sentence one says what you set out to do.
Sentence two says what your pages show.
Sentence three starts with the words I learnt.
Name a mark, a tool or a number in it.
A word like better is too soft to check.
Then write your locator on the last line.
File, page, box, and today's date.
Nobody writes this summary for you.
An adult may write your words down, and only your words.

items: Supported · copy the measure, ring met, part met or not met, and say one thing you learnt out loud.
Standard · copy the measure, ring the result, write three sentences, and name the file, page and box.
Stretch · as Standard, and write the next measure you would set, with a number in it.

blocks.text: If you finish early, check your locator points at one box.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: Sign and date each sheet yourself, in front of the pupil, and read their three sentences back unchanged.

blocks.text: Read it to an adult, then file it
Read your three sentences to the adult at your table.
They read them back to you, word for word.
If that is not what you meant, say it again.
They write the new words down as you say them.
Then the adult writes their name and the date.
That adult is your audience today.
Your words told them where to look.
Your sheet goes into the Part A section of the folder.
It goes in the folder, not in your bag.

Three sentences in your own words, the third starting with I learnt

checks: The measure on the sheet matches the week one skill card word for word.
One of met, part met or not met is ringed, and the last box on the strip supports it.
Three sentences are in the pupil's own words, and the third names a mark, a tool or a number.
The locator names a file, a page and a box, and carries today's date.
